consumers.reads: writes every file here and re-runs every case on --check
runs minimal/verify.py against these bytes and compares to the producer expectation
cites this directory when auditing which lane produced what; reads no field by name

THE FRONT DOOR. Runs verify.py against every case and prints the scoreboard a stranger sees first. It reads isHonestLog and does NOT derive a rule from integrity — it derived its own once and got 3 where this file got 7, for the same phrase.
THE STRANGER PATH — takes retained.json and presented.json as arguments and names no directory. Checked by INVOCATION in the stranger run, never by grep.

derivedQuestions.expectsAppendOnly: is a clean pass the CORRECT answer? true only for intact under a canonical encoding. A smaller set, and a different question.
derivedQuestions.isHonestLog: did the LOG do anything wrong? true for intact, damaged and malformed. The denominator of the false-accusation rate, and the stronger claim.

encodingCasesAreDeliberatelyNonCanonical: Cases with encoding "non-canonical" VIOLATE the rule above on purpose — they are the demonstration of what the rule is for. The gate exempts exactly those and no others.

fieldEncodings.firstUnverifiedLine: canonical integer literal, or the literal null
fieldEncodings.root: 64 lowercase hex characters, checked as characters and not by a decoder
fieldEncodings.treeSize: CANONICAL INTEGER LITERAL in the raw bytes: /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/ and at most 9007199254740991. No exponent, no fraction, no leading zero, no sign. `integer` is not a constraint JSON can express — 7, 7.0 and 7e0 are one type and three tokens, and after the parse the difference is unrecoverable. Checked against the TEXT, never the parse.

fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.demonstratorVerdict: the split cases only — what the other reader said, for a human comparing them
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.expectsAppendOnly: the second question, named so nobody re-derives it. No machine reads it today
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.note: the sentence a stranger reads beside the case; no gate parses it
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.presentedSize: orientation for a reader scanning the index
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.proofNodes: orientation; the proof itself is in presented.json
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.retainedSize: orientation for a reader scanning the index
fieldsWrittenForTheHumanReader.retainedSizeIsPowerOfTwo: derivable from retainedSize, published so a reader need not compute it

integrityValues.damaged: AN HONEST LOG whose proof was damaged in transport — one node zeroed. UNDETERMINED is the correct answer; a pass here would be the defect.
integrityValues.forged: a deliberate forgery. Not an honest log.
integrityValues.intact: nothing was tampered with. The log is honest AND a clean pass is the correct answer.
integrityValues.malformed: AN HONEST LOG whose root arrived malformed — 63 hex instead of 64. UNDETERMINED is correct.

malformedCasesAreUnreadable: Cases with integrity "malformed" carry a deliberately invalid root and are REFUSED by the strict reader. That is the point: a demo that can only contain inputs it already accepts is the closed loop that hid the malformed class from every harness in this repository.
presentedFields: proofFromPrevious (the consistency proof; the field name minimal/verify.py reads)
what: The declared contract for docs/heads/demo/. Emitted by scripts/head-emit.ts --demo and enforced by --check. An undeclared file in this directory, a missing field, or a listed consumer that no longer mentions the directory each take the gate red.
